decks.purpose: A modular chat application, a backend edge, and reusable workspace libraries.
The React application that assembles reusable features into a coherent workspace.
The NestJS edge that authenticates users, persists conversations and adapts DIAL Core.
A real browser host for exercising the chat overlay protocol.
A separate-origin HTML bridge for the MCP Apps double-iframe boundary.
Preview heterogeneous content through one typed surface.
Turn file state into clear attachment controls.
Give entity editors a shared structure and validation vocabulary.
Browse deployments and reusable assets without owning their storage.
Generate typed operations from the backend OpenAPI contract.
Reuse headless request lifecycles and chat-interface behavior.
Embed a running chat with a typed message protocol.
Share domain vocabulary, utilities and common UI primitives.
Compose a message with deployment, attachment and voice controls.
Render a transcript from host-owned messages and actions.
Navigate a large conversation history with a small visible list.
Make streamed execution progress visible inside a response.
Connect tool-result UI resources to an inline interactive preview.
Reuse navigation destinations across desktop and mobile chrome.
Author reusable prompt content while leaving persistence to the host.
Pick reusable prompts and collect their parameter values.
Reuse the publish-to-folder workflow across different entity types.
Connect answer annotations to inspectable evidence.
Render task lists, forms and run history from host-owned schedules.
Provide accessible vertical selection for settings pages.
Present a share link and access choices without issuing the link.
Give feature panels a common resizable shell.
Edit a skill and its supporting file tree through host callbacks.
Select a reusable skill without coupling the picker to sending.
Put uploaded files, generated files and citations in one evidence panel.
Offer prompt starters that fit the available space.
Coordinate MCP toolset editing through an explicit host adapter.
Explain cost and model limits using normalized display data.
